name: Guest suite in Asheville · ★4.88 · 1 bedroom · 2 beds · 1 bath
neighborhood_overview: Our beautiful Grove Park Historic District close to downtown is a safe, friendly neighborhood with well-lit sidewalks, wonderful gardens, parks, and a fantastic greenway linking to the center of Asheville.
host_about:
Welcome to Terrace Cottage!

For fifteen years we have enjoyed hosting visitors in our Asheville, North Carolina cottage from across the country and around the world including England and Ireland, Greece, Canada, Mexico and Cuba, Argentina, Japan and The Phillipines. We welcome guests from around the corner, across the US and our international visitors as well! Our college-age daughter grew up listening to many different languages in the driveway.

We enjoy traveling including work-and-play trips to Ireland, England, Sweden and Greece. Twenty years here at our residence built in 1926 and our adjacent Terrace Cottage was built in 2000.

We love working in our perennial beds and veggie gardens.

I'm an online entrepreneur designing and marketing wooden playthings for young people. I also collect and blog about vintage wooden toys.

My wife is a clinician with UNC-Chapel Hill School of Medicine. 

We love living in Asheville and are always happy to return home when away. It is a nationally-celebrated and uniquely beautiful mountain city overflowing with eclectic opportunities for enjoying first-rate dining, entertainment, crafts and artwork. The Blue Ridge Parkway entrance is ten minutes from our home, leading to the North Carolina Arboretum, Mount Pisgah, Craggy Gardens, and Mount Mitchell- the highest elevation east of the Rocky Mountains. 

I fly fish and welcome inquiries regarding our local waters. My favorite streams are under an hour away and have been rated in Trout Unlimited's Top 100. There are excellent fly shops and outfitters nearby if you need them.

Walking, running and cycling are huge in Asheville and there are too many options to mention from neighborhood greenways and hill climbs to maniacal day-longs as well, contact us for info. Our local runner's and cyclist's shops are just blocks away.

Speaking of walkable- ditto our supermarket and specialty/whole foods markets, cafes, coffee shops, local theater, pharmacies, UNC-Asheville, botanical gardens, awesome kid's parks and more.

Thanks for looking at Terrace Cottage and we welcome your inquiries!

name: Bungalow in Asheville · ★4.90 · 1 bedroom · 1 bed · 1 private bath
neighborhood_overview:
From a local real estate website: "West Asheville is an area that moves easily between its old-world history and new-world energy, enjoying the charm of its neighborhoods and the spirit of its quaint main street. It's both down-to-earth and cutting-edge, with 1920's bungalows and eco-built new homes, with old brick buildings that house innovative businesses, with appreciation for its stories and excitement for its future."

And from the "Explore Asheville" website: "West Asheville's funky vibe translates into a varied mix of eateries. Happening on this unique neighborhood leaving downtown Asheville, you encounter boutiques and cafés lining Haywood Avenue. This West Asheville hub of activity is in the midst of a neighborhood renaissance."
host_about:
I first came to Asheville 2003 and after a five-year stint teaching at Warren Wilson College, I moved two hours away because of a new job only to return five more years later. Perhaps it has something to do with the "vortex" in Asheville that some folks here talk about but probably more to do with the relationships that I have cultivated here, the people and their values, the mountains that surround us, the great climate, the restaurants and bookstores. 
I was born and raised in Malaysia but have lived longer in the United States than I have in Asia now. I have traveled a bit, to Asia - 5 trips to Tibet, 4 to India, 6 to China, several to Taiwan, Thailand, Bhutan other Asian countries, and in recent years I’ve spent quite a bit of time in Guatemala, Peru, and Mexico. Back in college I traveled to a sprinkling of European countries. I've also lived a year in London and loved it. I'm a hybrid of quiet and gregarious, easy-going with others and meticulous with myself. I don't smoke, I'm not into mind-altering substances and I don't drink (but don't have a problem with others drinking). I spend a lot of time at a West Asheville, spiritual (Buddhist) center but I am capable of talking about things other than meditation and mindfulness!  Especially food. And food.

(See my guidebook for other recommendations.)
Other walkable restaurants and venues include Westville Pub, The Oyster House Brewery, One World Brewery, The Whale, and The Walk. Other favorites are Nine Mile, The Universal Joint, Sunny Point, and Dobra Tea.

I lived in Europe for two years and have subsequently traveled extensively, mostly in Central and South America.  I am a Spanish teacher and musician and love to work with children and adults.  I practice yoga, love to read, dance, eat out, and socialize, and feel fortunate to have wound up in this great city of Asheville with my fascinating and fabulous daughter.

host_about:
Hello! My husband and I are looking forward to hosting guests in our home as well as being a guest of others during our travels. We became AirBnB hosts in 2014 and have since hosted more than 2,000 bookings. In 2018, we became AirBnB superhosts!

We live in Asheville in the beautiful mountains of western North Carolina.

Allison works as a fourth grade teacher at Mills River Elementary School. Peter works as the Trails Coordinator at a regional land trust, Conserving Carolina. Both of us work to keep this region we love as wonderful as it is today, and make it even better for future generations.

We love to take road trips throughout the year. We have appreciated the kindness of many over the years who have let us stay in their home or camp in their yard, or have rented a room to us for a reasonable rate. We are guests who are focused on our travels and we most often are seeking simply a room to hang our hat for the night before our travels resume the following morning. For that reason, most hosts barely know that we are there. In appreciation for the kindness shown to us over the years, we pay it forward by being clean and courteous when we are guests in the homes of others, and we are seeking to host guests who are similarly self-sufficient and simply seeking a basic place for the night.

We look forward to you staying in our home!

name: Place to stay in Asheville · ★4.94 · 1 bedroom · 1 bed · 1 private bath
neighborhood_overview:
Since I grew up on Cherry Lane, in the house next door, I have many fond and magical memories. Today, it still holds that magic. It's a family centered neighborhood and folks appreciate slow driving on Cherry Lane's small street as there are kids who actually play outside!
My grandparents bought the three acres in 1945 because a double rainbow hung over the eastern view. 10 Cherry Lane was where they lived until my family moved in with them. Four kids and two parents living in the upstairs at 10 had my grandparents moving quickly to build their dream house. 12 was designed by a protege of Frank Lloyd Wright and is a one-of-a-kind style with plenty of light and outside areas for calm meditative moments or kickball. A garden provides fresh heirloom tomatoes, herbs, beans, corn and squash you are welcome to enjoy and use if cooking.

If you want to walk to places, there's a few great restaurants less than a mile away. Moe's Barbaque is down the hill, Cecelia's Argentinian
host_about:
My grandparents built this house in 1959. My grandfather was a Major General, head of the 13th AD, and a graduate of West Point in 1915, along with Eisenhower and Omar Bradley. After getting shot in WW2, his military career ended and he and my grandmother moved to Asheville so he could run the VA Hospital in Oteen. 

The house next door and three acres is what they bought in 1945 after witnessing a double rainbow over the mountains. After my mother and father moved us four kids to the upstairs of that house, my grandparents got an architect who studied with Frank Lloyd Wright to design the mid-century modern house next door, and my childhood was spent going between the houses. 

Four years ago I came up to renovate the place in order to sell it, but after watching a full moon rise over the mountains, I fell in love with it all over again and bought it. It's a comfort knowing this property has never left our family. I can feel all my relations here and enjoy the memories I had, mostly with my loving, brilliant, funny grandmother in this house. It has been a gathering spot for many famous people, including Ike and Mamie, who were close friends of my grandparents, and Carl Sandburg. 

I am an artistic welder and a singer and have travelled all over the world entertaining the troops for the Dept of Defense. Along the path of my travels, I always appreciated the kindness of locals who guided me when lost or recommended flavorful local places set apart from the tourist track. I'm here to offer you the same guidance.

There are sculptures and furniture inside and around my property that I made. 

 I love meeting new people, and I also love my privacy. I respect guests privacy as well and am available with any questions, concerns, interests you may have, but otherwise will not intrude. I live upstairs, and I am sensitive to being quiet. I encourage my guests to feel right at home. 

The expansive yard has plenty of areas to sit and enjoy a cup of coffee or a cocktail. The garden beds have herbs you are welcome to use.

Feel free to text with any questions prior to your stay as well as during your stay. My goal is for everyone who books the studio to enjoy the view, the birds, the wildlife, and the close proximity to everything fun while feeling far away, so much so, that they want to come back!!!

neighborhood_overview:
We live in Oak Park in a cluster of historic houses south of downtown Asheville. Our property is one of six houses that surrounds a one acre park where you will regularly find families practicing baseball and soccer and neighbors running with their dogs amidst the towering oak trees that give the neighborhood its name. Our home was previously owned by a large loving family who ran a greenhouse on the adjacent property which now houses a family owned Hispanic Market. A distinctive feature of our home is the Christmas tree planted by the former family in the front yard over 40 years ago that now towers over the house. We fully remodeled and lovingly restored the interior of our home in 2003, including building the apartment in the former carriage "house" space. We are now working on finishing the exterior (just paint, no noisy tools!). Tim is a general contractor and I am an artist. This space is a beautiful collaboration of both of our strengths.
Great convenience to the Asheville
host_about: Transplants from Southern California in 1992 we have loved raising our family in the Asheville area. Our eldest, a daughter, was married in 2015 and lives with her husband (who works for Sierra Nevada) and our grandson in the Hendersonville area. Our middle son lives and works in downtown Asheville and our youngest son is a 2020 graduate from our small private school and is headed to college in the fall. Tim is a licensed general contractor and insurance adjuster. Elisa is an artist and art teacher at a PK-12 private school. We have restored multiple historic properties in the Asheville area over the last 24 years including a condemned house in the Montford Historic District for which Tim won the prestigious Griffin Award for historic preservation in 2004. Our commitment to faithful restoration is apparent in this property which we fully remodeled and restored in 2003. We have been landlords for several long term rentals in the area for 29 years, including this apartment, and have enjoyed the transition to vacation rental. We love both stimulating and laid back conversation with our friends and appropriate mood music (we can't live without our Bose Sounddock or Sonos), good food (esp Mexican) and craft beer and wine. Our love of the outdoors takes us to California's Yosemite National Park for camping every summer and to our family condo on the gulf coast as often as we can get there. We enjoy hiking and biking and late night fire pits. We can point you to the usual and the unusual spots in Asheville so just ask. We can make a church recommendation if that's important to you. We think we have the best friends in the world and we especially love making new ones. We look forward to your visit!

Historic Montford, one the oldest neighborhoods (and in my humble opinion, the most beautiful), is a block away and the architecture is truly inspiring. My favorite coffee shop sits at the bottom of the street, called High Five Cafe. Don't let the hip tattooed baristas intimidate you- the coffee is delicious! name: Guest suite in Asheville · ★4.90 · Studio · 1 bed · 1 bath
neighborhood_overview:

Whether you like to eat well in or out, our neighborhood is home to Whole Foods, Trader Joe's and Harris Teeter, in addition to the many delicious, local restaurants.

Discover all downtown has to offer. On your leisurely walks, you will see the charming Craftsman style homes of our neighborhood give way to a quirky mix of original Art Deco, Beaux Arts and Neoclassical styles downtown. Stop and listen to any number of talented street musicians and entertainers along your path. Asheville is home to a strong local business culture, featuring locally-owned restaurants and coffee shops, shopping boutiques, and more than 30 art galleries.
host_about:
Asheville's unofficial motto: "Don't postpone joy"

Six things I can't live without: stars, books, good people, good food, my compass, and my kitties.

My favorite restaurants in Asheville: Plant, Laughing Seed, Mayfel's.

Best places to sit, sip, nibble and dream: The Battery Park Book Exchange, High Five Coffee, Dobra Tea House, The Coffee Bus, Vortex Donuts, Malaprops bookstore.

I'll see anything that's playing at: the Fine Arts Movie Theater, the Mothlight music venue.

If it's your first visit to Asheville, don't miss: a hike on the Blue Ridge Parkway, a sunset drink at the Skybar, the LaZoom Comedy Bus Tour, a roots drink at Noble Kava, the vegan donuts at Vortex, and amazing snackage at the Gourmet Chip Company.

My husband and I are natives of Asheville.  We love this vibrant city and the beautiful mountains of WNC and love sharing our knowledge and experiences with you.  

I am an artist/educator with a home studio adjacent to Bluebirds Nest.  My paintings are in a gallery in the River Arts District at 310 ART where I have taught workshops. I would be glad to recommend sites and galleries to see while visiting Asheville.

I am a retired teacher from Buncombe County Schools.  National Board Certified, I taught digital imaging, website development, and computer applications.  

My interest in digital imaging led me into photography with the beauty of these WNC mountains and the people and their culture being my favorite subjects.

I come from a railroading family and Southern Railway/Norfolk Southern has been good to us.  The railroad's history is tied to the River Arts District and I felt as if I was "coming home" when I became an exhibiting artist at 310 ART at Riverview Station.

My husband comes from a Coca-Cola family who pioneered Coke in the western most counties including Bryson City.  His aunt married into the Granville Calhoun family and the old homeplace is still standing up Hazel Creek in the Great Smokies National Park.

I enjoy hiking and fishing but my waterskiing days are over!  We especially like to spend long weekends at our houseboat on Fontana Lake with our family.

We have two wonderful daughters, son-in-laws, and three red-headed grandchildren!  

We will be glad to share our knowledge of this area with you and make any recommendations you may be interested in.

Our style of hosting is very simple.  We are here if you need us and want to provide you with the best accommodations possible.  We want you to feel as if you are family.

We invite you to stay with us and hope to see you soon.

Bet

There are three neighborhood eateries, which include Nine Mile (Caribbean cuisine), Tall Johns (Euro-American), and All Day Darling (casual breakfast/lunch/dinner).

The Asheville Visitor's Center is in Montford and only an 8-minute walk from our house.

New Belgium Brewery and River Arts District (RAD) are less than 2 miles away, West Asheville is 3 miles, and Biltmore Estate is about 5 miles down the road.

Connecting deeply with Nature and animals, and with open-minded people is my delight.

A special note about the name Llamasté.....when I had the good fortune to become the Steward of this blessed mountain sanctuary, there were two llamas and two goats living here who clearly stated their preference to stay put, rather than go with their previous  beloved owners to much smaller and less green pastures. neighborhood_overview:
Location, Location, Location
If you’ve ever wandered through downtown Asheville, then you’ve felt the wanderlust (and “wonder-lust)” of N. Lexington Avenue.

This is the most hip and quintessential street in Asheville – a place where restaurants go unadvertised and the best bars have no signs, just a door. This is a place where high-end art galleries abut record shops, upscale shoe stores, and more.

And, while Real Life may be about compromise – sacrifice This to get That – we believe that vacation should be a special time. A time you get both This and That, no compromise required.

80 LEX is your no-compromise-required destination: both urban and urbane, situated right in the beating heart of our vibrant city. Enveloped by the energy and excitement of downtown life, Unit 201 embodies and embraces the Asheville scene – a scene that draws designers and artists, creatives and music lovers, foodies and artisanal beverage aficionados alike.
host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

name: Rental unit in Asheville · ★4.99 · 1 bedroom · 1 bed · 1 bath
neighborhood_overview: The property sits on a quintessential street in Asheville – a place where restaurants go unadvertised and the best bars have no signs; just a door. This is a place where high-end art galleries abut record shops, upscale shoe stores, and more.
host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

The two of us met in Aspen, CO. Heather is originally from Chicago and Mark from Virginia Beach. Although Heather loved city life her wanderlust brought her to Aspen for thirteen years. Mark has opened his own office and Heather teaches at a creative arts center while studying interior design. Besides continuing to travel, we hike with our son and two dogs as often as possible and love checking out the awesome breweries and restaurants Asheville has to offer. We hope to inspire others to get out of their comfort zone and check out other places and people on this amazing planet! 

"Not until we are lost do we begin to understand ourselves." 
- Henry David Thoreau

host_about:
Our houses are much nicer than they appear on this site.   Airbnb does not allow us to use our own photographs on two of our listings so you may need to go on our internal website.   It is easy to find us with a simple search for "Upstream way"   That is the name of our street.

We also have lots of cool video and virtual tours.   Lesley, my right hand, has compiled volumes of information on Asheville and travel tips for your visit.

Anyone who uses Airbnb knows you have to invest a lot of time and energy to find the good rentals in Asheville, NC.   The city made it illegal after we got our permits and there are way too many folks trying to book far too few homes.    

We built our new website so you will not get tricked with photoshop.    Our 5 houses on Upstream Way are the real thing.   

My development company built the whole street so we are not like a normal house you find in a random location next door to owner occupied homes in a residential neighborhood.   

I have stayed in those before and you are not exactly welcomed by the other homeowners.   The neighbors tend to dislike the constant coming and going of tourists in a family neighborhood.

I once lived next to an illegal Airbnb property and came up with a solution.

We are literally an entire resort of vacation rentals all side by side.   Your neighbor is also here for a special occasion and will probably offer you a beverage.

You can bring anywhere from 1 to 100 people and have the whole place to yourself.

It is without equal.   The best you can do is copy us, but nobody can get the permits.

Bachelorette’s and Wedding Parties got us started but we shy away from them now.   

We will host a lot of different occasions and you need not worry if you want to have a bachelor party or bachelorette.   

I make it no secret that we want to focus on corporate executives who visit for team building and holistic health retreats, but we don't judge your motive.

We welcome everyone the same way.

You can depend on us because we deliver what you are expecting and then we go as far beyond as is humanly possible.

My team has some of the best and brightest.   My right hand is Lesley, my left hand is Aracely, her children Kasey and Brian are her right and left hands.  If something needs repair, Leo & Kaden are available.

I have known each person on my staff from years and years of time together.   I am not easy to work for.   Trust me.   

At times, I have no idea why these people are such hard workers and trusted friends. 
With Covid-19 we all work for a fraction of our former compensation.

Somehow; you and I both got lucky.    We survived this and I see the light at the end of the tunnel.

Ok, I will wrap this up:

If you reach out you will never get an answering service or a stranger.   

We are not property managers.    We are the folks who built this place.

We built it for you.

You don't arrive here by accident.

So far, 217 Airbnb customers have reviewed us.   Keep in mind, that represents thousands of people as our average group is 12 people.

Nobody has ever given us below 5 stars.   Not even once.   Not even close.

Plus, you are welcome to check a lot of other websites and our own internal software.  

Thousands of people have come here and they seem to be happy with us and we often see them again and again.

We cost more for a reason:   

You get more.

You come for a special occasion.   

You leave with a priceless memory.

Then we plan for the next one.

I think that is why we are almost booked out into '22.

All the best,
jay

Born in NC, attended UNC-Chapel Hill and got a degree in Journalism. My mom's side of the family has lived in Western North Carolina for the past century and a half. I have relatives buried in the Riverside Cemetery, which we can see from our backyard.
However, I lived most of my adult life on the West Coast. After college, I drove west in a school bus and eventually landed outside Eugene, OR, next to a creek, grew lots of my food, and had a sewing business, selling at the Saturday Market, Circle of Hands and craft fairs up and down the West Coast.
I have been to all 50 states, Canada, several Central American countries, Caribbean islands and Europe. I LOVE meeting people from all around the world and have studied conflict resolution in large groups of people using World Work. I am a therapist full time, offering massage therapy as well as Bodywisdom Therapy, helping people unravel the messages of their bodies, at a location on Merrimon Avenue. I speak a bit of French and Spanish, but am alas, no longer fluent.
My son and I moved back to WNC several years ago to be near my Mom, who lives in Yancey County. I know some sweet areas to visit around the area and are including them in a notebook in the rooms. 
I love being able to offer people a centrally located place to enjoy what WNC has to offer, as well as a prime walking neighborhood to have access to downtown Asheville hotspots. 
I turned both bedrooms and bathrooms downstairs into places that I would like to visit myself, using art from my own collection, and textures and colors that I love.
We have friends and family over on a regular basis so there is a bit of hustle and bustle at times. If you have children, or like to come and go and appreciate the outdoors, you will fit right in! If you want privacy, the private entrance and keypad will fit your needs. If you want total peace and quiet, I am afraid we won't be your cup of tea.
Living lightly on the earth is a core value for me so we recycle as much as possible, and keep our throwaway consumables to a minimum. 
Life is for loving, sharing and making the world better wherever we can.

Come masquerade as a local and enjoy the short walk to the dozens of popular dining, music, shopping and people watching activities Haywood Rd. has to offer. Though quite close to downtown, 100 years ago West Asheville was its own town independent of Asheville. As a result, this unique area of town has its own “Mini-Downtown” that is centered around Haywood Rd. For the last few decades this commercial corridor has enjoyed a period of reinvestment by the community and area businesses. Several cool and unique restaurants, coffee shops, bars, bakeries, breweries and shops have chosen West Asheville as their home. Century old houses are being renovated back to life and new homes are being built on every available lot. As the historic town of “West Asheville” was never very big, the entire area is very walkable and there are lots of cool old buildings, churches, trees and houses.
The River Arts District and New Belgium Brewing are a 5 minute drive, Biltmore Estate is a 15 minute drive

LOCATION, LOCATION, LOCATION!
If you’ve ever wandered through downtown Asheville, then you’ve felt the wanderlust (and “wonder-lust)” of this historic warren.

Here, connecting two of the city’s most sought-after streets – W. Walnut and Woodfin/Hiawassee – Carolina Lane is a quiet (for the city) alley, long known to the real Asheville. This is where Oscar winning actress Frances McDormond conspicuously smoked her cigarettes after a day of filming in the area and industry once reigned. And this neighborhood? Well, it’s still a place where restaurants go unadvertised and the best bars have no signs, just a door. A place where high-end art galleries about record shops, upscale shoe stores, and more.

And, while Real Life may be about compromise – sacrifice This to get That – we believe that vacation should be a special time. A time you get both This and That, no compromise required.

35 Caroline Lane is your no-compromise-required destination: both urban
host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

The Montford Area Historic District is one of the prettiest neighborhoods in the country--though we're admittedly a little biased. Most of the neighborhood's residences were constructed between 1890 and 1920 in the Victorian or Queen Anne Victorian styles, though you'll also find architecture in the Arts and Crafts, Neoclassical, and Colonial Revival styles. Residents pride themselves on their gardening and landscaping expertise, benefited in no small part by the region's capacity for growing an incredible diversity of flora, from the signature magnolia trees, to flowering shrubs like the rhododendron & azalea, to bamboo, succulents, and so much more.

The gorgeous local cemetery is worth a visit, marking the final resting place of authors Thomas Wolfe and O. Henry. North Montford was once home to the Highland Hospital, in which Zelda Fitzgerald tragically died in a fire in 1948.

Located in East Asheville in the 28805 zip code, Haw Creek was named for the native Black Haw shrub or small tree (Viburnum prunifolium) that grew more abundantly years ago along the moist soils of the valley, especially along Haw Creek itself.

Haw Creek valley’s southern boundary extends from US Highway 70/Tunnel Road at I-240 eastward along Tunnel Road to Maple Springs Road. Its west boundary is formed by Piney Mountain/Bear Mountain ridge; Town Mountain creates the northern boundary; and the Blue Ridge Parkway stretches along most of its eastern border.

Haw Creek was settled in the early 1800’s as a farming community with the first school established in 1842 on the site of the present day Bethesda Cemetery. Haw Creek has two main entrances with very narrow roads throughout the valley. host_about:
Emilie first fell in love with Asheville over 20 years ago when she attended Rockbrook Camp in the heart of a wooded mountain in Brevard, NC. Those mountains, so different from the beaches of her childhood, kept her coming back for ten years. There is something majestic about the Blue Ridge Mountains that blanket Western North Carolina, at over 1 billion years old, they are some of the oldest mountains in the entire world.

Arturo came to Asheville for the first time in 2012 and was quickly enamoured with the outdoor culture, so different from his 22 years in New York City, but so reminiscent of his childhood in the gentle hills of Puebla, Mexico. For him, it was a desire to start a family and a business and seek a better quality of life and he quickly found himself thirsty for everything that Asheville has to offer.

Emilie and Arturo met in 2008 while working together as sommeliers in the Lower East Side of Manhattan at The Ten Bells. Their working relationship was incredible, and over the next six years that relationship became a fine tuned machine- customers would always comment about the way they were able to seamlessly run the entire restaurant without even speaking. Learning the way one another worked over those first six years was the beginning of a true friendship that blossomed into love.

With 35 years of fine dining experience between the two, a Bed and Breakfast seemed like the perfect next adventure. Their penchant for hospitality and intuitive service and their true joy in meeting new people and making new friends put them in a unique position to choose their next path.

Emilie’s first Bed and Breakfast plan was written in the back of a college notebook when she was 18, wandering around Maine searching for the perfect wraparound porch. In 2011, she and Arturo decided to give those Bed and Breakfast dreams a trial run, and opened a small B&B in their East Village apartment. While tiny, it gave them a wonderful test-run on breakfast planning, scheduling, cleaning, decorating, recipe testing and conflict management. They loved it all!

The tri-lingual couple feel that they will bring a new, re-invented experience to the somewhat clichéd country B&B Inn. Asheville is no longer a sleepy town with boarded up buildings, it is a hub of restaurants, nightlife, music, beer and outdoor adventure. It’s not only the perfect place to call home, it is the perfect place to welcome someone into yours.

A little historical fact about Kenilworth area for your reference:
Per the kenilworthresidentsassociation.org site, Kenilworth, touted as Asheville’s 'Pioneer Suburb,' was founded in 1914. Situated on high land above the Swannanoa River, Kenilworth is one of Asheville’s oldest neighborhoods and was once its own town before getting annexed by the City of Asheville in 1929.

Just across the French Broad River from downtown, West Asheville (28806) is a mecca for originality. For the past few years, people have flocked to this funky neighborhood, either to visit or buy a quaint cottage within walking distance of the many new businesses that have opened in the area.

Haywood Road has been the main street of West Asheville for more than a century. Old buildings are now home to modern businesses, but the street still has a small hometown feel. As you walk down the street, you will see old buildings renovated for new businesses side-by-side with second- and third-generation shops. There are now many restaurants, breweries, pubs with frequent live music, bakeries, a variety of resale consignment shops, vintage clothing boutiques and even a half-dozen record shops lining the road that appeal to visitors interested in sampling the unique, bohemian flavor of Asheville.

Come and experience for yourself why residents love calling Asheville home.

neighborhood_overview:
The Nonagon is conveniently located in South Asheville close to Lake Julian, and is a quick 8 minute drive from the Asheville Regional Airport. Downtown Asheville and the Biltmore Estates are only 11 miles away, and The Blue Ridge Parkway can be easily accessed as well. Take advantage of our close proximity to Lake Julian, which offers fishing, walking trails, disc golf, and paddle boat rentals.
Coming for adventure? Float the French Broad River with Beer City Tubing, located a quick 1 mile away. Or, check out The Riveter, which is only 4 miles away and boasts an indoor climbing gym, a bike park, and a yoga studio.
Looking for some great breweries? Spend some time at the one of a kind Sierra Nevada brewery, check out 12 Bones or Voodoo Brewing, or head downtown and explore the South Slope!
You'll also be well positioned to enjoy some of the area's more popular trails, such as Triple Falls in DuPont State Forest, or Looking Glass in Pisgah Forest.
